objective: Help owners of large scientific PDF collections test versions, extraction, citations, retrieval, and provenance before committing to whole-collection RAG or knowledge-graph work.

source_needs.problem: A multilingual collection of more than 300 PDFs needs a fully local retrieval design rather than another unmeasured stack recommendation.
A scientific collection of roughly 17,000 PDFs needs local ingestion, reliable citations, and a design that can be maintained as the library changes.

lazyblog.content: A complete collection-integrity workflow covers source ledgers, version families, extraction classes, page-level citation contracts, lexical baselines, provenance-bearing graph edges, incremental updates, and an owner-defined acceptance boundary before one quiet LKT fit-check route.
lazyblog.policy: The guide solves the collection-design problem before mentioning the maintained LKT offer. It makes no whole-collection accuracy, customer-result, turnaround, lead, or revenue claim.
